Subject: Trial extension request for Novatech evaluation

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the intro call earlier. We were hoping to get a short trial extension for our engineering team — we ran into scheduling slippage and only just started a heavier test of the Redwood Dedicated demo.

We've previously used a pair of short trial credits (two separate accounts last quarter) while evaluating different teams. If possible could we get an additional 7 days on the main workspace to finish the evaluation? Happy to sign an evaluation agreement if that helps.

Attached: purchase_order.pdf (stub)

Best,
Alex Turner

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the note. I can loop in Rishi and our internal ops to look at the account history. To move quickly, can you confirm:
- The primary account email/HubSpot record for the workspace you want extended
- Whether the previous two trials were run under distinct legal entities or under the same org (we sometimes see repeated signups linked back to the same paying org)

I'll aim to get a quick-eyes fraud check today and follow up with next steps. If there are compliance or procurement docs you can share, drop them here or upload to the Drive link.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-07T09:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Trial extension request for Novatech evaluation

On Thu, May 6, 2026 at 11:02 Soojin Lee wrote:
> Hi Alex —
>
> Thanks for the note...

Quick summary from my side after a preliminary check:
- I pulled the account history and found three recent trial-related events tied to domain novatech.ai across two HubSpot records.
- Two of those records were granted short credits in Feb and Mar; one of the signups reused a disposable email pattern.
- There are multiple device fingerprints and overlapping IP ranges that look like repeat evaluations from the same engineering group but created as distinct workspaces.

I attached a csv with the signups flagged (suspicious-signups.csv) and the open support ticket (support_ticket_3456.pdf). My recommendation: do not auto-grant another open-ended credit. If Soojin wants to support the deal, offer a monitored 7-day extension tied to constrained usage (cap tokens/day) and require an evaluation form + signed trial agreement. Escalate to security if they request more credits or new accounts.

Suggested outbound to Novatech (editable):
"Hi Alex — we can grant a one-week monitored extension with a daily token cap while we complete a short compliance check. We'll need a signed evaluation agreement. If you can confirm the primary HubSpot record and legal entity, I will route the agreement"

Thoughts?
-Rishi

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@novatech.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-09T17:52:00Z
Subject: Re: Trial extension request for Novatech evaluation

Alex —

Thanks for your patience. After a brief internal review we can approve a 7-day monitored extension for the workspace you referenced. Conditions:
- Daily token cap of 150k tokens (to prevent broad reuse)
- A signed evaluation agreement (attached)
- No additional credit will be issued to other workspaces without a manual commercial review

If you agree, sign the attached trial_extension_agreement.txt and reply; we'll enable the extension and monitor usage. If you anticipate exceeding the cap, please let us know and we'll engage sales ops + security for a commercial plan review.

On our side, Rishi will keep an eye on signups and flag repeat patterns — Marissa, can you log a short monitoring task in the account?

Best,
